headline: Approved March 26, 2026 meeting minutes as amended; reviewed draft Economic Development Action Plan strategy framework.
summary: The Council approved the March 26, 2026 meeting minutes as amended. Consultant Sam Eisenbeiser of BerryDunn presented the draft Economic Development Action Plan, covering the vision, goals, strategic objectives, target sectors, and five strategy groups, and outlined next steps for finalizing the plan. The group also discussed future agenda topics such as the housing network and school items.
decisions: Approved the March 26, 2026 meeting minutes as amended, 9-0.

2. Sam Eisenbeiser, BerryDunn, Economic Development Action Plan 28 
 29 
Sam Eisenbeiser, BerryDunn, explained that the process kicked off in August of last year 30 
beginning with data collection and market analysis, followed by a stakeholder engagement 31 
meeting in October. The stakeholder engagement was robust and included a community wide 32 
survey, a survey of major employers, focused group discussions and interviews, and a 33 
community open house event in February. The design of the process was intended to ground the 34 
strategy in both data and local input and feedback. The process is now at the point of formulating 35 
the Economic Development strategy. The next phase will be to convert that framework into the 36 
detailed Action Plan itself. The starting point for the work is the Economic Development Vision 37 
that was established through outreach and planning work in 2021. The vision is about sustaining 38 
a vibrant and diverse economy that includes a spectrum of large employers, startups, and small 39 
businesses across the key sectors. There are five goals to support the vision, as articulated in Plan 40 
Beverly: expanding the tax base, quality jobs, diversifying industry, business support, and 41 
sustainability and identity. These goals provide the foundation and the justification for 42 
everything that follows. The analysis and engagement pointed to a very consistent set of themes 43 
and findings in Beverly with many assets, such as a strong business base, valuable downtown 44 
and waterfront assets, educational institutions, a highly educated workforce, and meaningful 45

industry and business activity which is also supported by entrepreneurship and innovation 46 
resources. The ability to take advantage of Beverly's assets to build economic resilience and 47 
more inclusive prosperity is being constrained by a set of persistent barriers, such as housing 48 
affordability, wage cost mismatch, childcare and other access barriers, mobility and parking 49 
issues, constrained land and infrastructure, and permitting complexity.  50 
 51 
Eisenbeiser stated that the strategic objectives include growing and diverse diversifying jobs and 52 
industry, expanding housing and livability, strengthening workforce talent and mobility, 53 
strengthening downtown and key districts, improving competitiveness and site readiness, in 54 
advancing inclusive participation. These objectives are a bridge between the early analysis 55 
phases and the aspirational vision and goals  56 
 57 
Schaeffer asked if mobility refers to transportation mobility or people/job mobility. Eisenbeiser 58 
stated that there is some overlap. Workforce talent mobility is about facilitating the transactional 59 
nature of labor, as well as economy and commerce. Mobility provides the access needed to make 60 
sure people can get to their jobs and other elements of infrastructure  61 
 62 
Eisenbeiser explained that a suite of clusters was developed across the spectrum that included 63 
strong representation in terms of the momentum and the impact potential they have. These 64 
include advanced manufacturing and clean technology, the biosciences, and entrepreneurship in 65 
small scale manufacturing. These sectors matter because they combine an established local 66 
presence with meaningful potential to create quality jobs, tax base growth, and diversification. 67 
Beverly's future it's not designed to depend on one sector alone. This approach leverages the 68 
benefits of a balanced portfolio of anchor sectors, innovation sectors, and locally rooted 69 
economic activity. There is cross cutting support among all three sectors. Notably 70 
entrepreneurship can be supportive of the other two. 71 
 72 
There was discussion regarding trends and data in terms of which sectors have the least amount 73 
of infrastructure but the highest ceiling. Eisenbeiser stated that these three sectors each play a 74 
specific and unique role. Beverly already has a strong location quotient. It is important to keep 75 
the industries that already have a rooted presence growing and evolving but entrepreneurship has 76 
a high upside.  77 
 78 
Eisenbeiser explained that the strategies are organized into five groups in total. The first strategy 79 
group focuses on Beverly's productive economy. This includes the sectors, firms, and business 80 
conditions that drive job creation, attract private investment, and build tax based growth. This 81 
group combines advanced manufacturing support, bioscience support, business concierge 82 
functionality, incentive policy updates, and improvements to the permitting policy climate. These 83 
strategies are meant to make Beverly more competitive for firms and sectors that align well with 84 
the City's strengths.  85 
 86 
The second group focuses on site readiness and economic resilience. The key idea is that future 87 
growth will be constrained unless Beverly deliberately prepares land, infrastructure, and 88 
employment areas for the next stage of investment. This group includes planning for energy and 89 
grid capacity, expanding flexible industrial and starter facilities, using partnerships to improve 90

site readiness, protecting and upgrading job centers, and improving access to industrial areas. 91 
These items ensure that Beverly has the physical and infrastructure capacity to capture growth, 92 
rather than risk losing it to other surrounding areas.  93 
 94 
The third group is housing and workforce opportunity. It recognizes that the aims and goals of 95 
economic development go beyond business growth and site readiness. One essential item for 96 
economic development is whether people can live in the City and participate in the economy. 97 
The unifying theme across this group is opportunity and household stability. It includes childcare 98 
and workforce support, workforce housing, stronger career pathways. events to bridge funding 99 
gaps for smaller businesses, and targeted measures to improve economic mobility. The strategies 100 
are all connected by the simple premise that Beverly will be more competitive and more 101 
inclusive, as more residents and workers have access to the opportunities that the local economy 102 
is creating on a constant basis. 103 
 104 
The fourth group focuses on the parts of Beverly that clearly define its identity and the economic 105 
experience, including the downtown waterfront and key districts. The unifying theme is that 106 
Beverly does not need to create a new identity, but has opportunities to sharpen, connect, and 107 
strengthen the places that are present already. This group brings together waterfront business 108 
growth, arts and visitor economy, waterfront to downtown linkages, storefront readiness and 109 
business support, and infill and adaptive reuse to gather ideas designed to strengthen the district 110 
vitality and improve the visitor and resident experience. 111 
 112 
The fifth group focuses on who benefits from the growth and how the City is delivering results. 113 
The unifying theme is broader participation, meaningful coordination, and effective 114 
implementation. The strategies include inclusive opportunity access, talent pipeline coordination, 115 
external branding, creating community feedback loops, and economic development roundtable. 116 
This group focuses on the process needed to implement the strategies. To be effective, Beverly 117 
needs measures that expand participation, improve transparency, and build trust that public plans 118 
will lead to visible action over time.  119 
 120 
Success under the strategy looks like more quality jobs at a broader industry mix and stronger 121 
business retention information. Place success means investment-ready sites and stronger 122 
downtown commercial districts. With regard to the community, success means more housing and 123 
workforce stability, greater participation and opportunities, and more visible progress and 124 
stronger trust. 125 
 126 
There was discussion regarding how the arts, landscapers, tourism, etc. are included in the plan. 127 
Eisenbeiser stated that these aspects are woven in and can be addressed throughout areas in the 128 
plan.  129 
 130 
Eisenbeiser reviewed the next steps. Moving forward, the set of strategies which has established 131 
the direction will be finalized. This will then be translated into something that can be 132 
implemented. Once the strategies are finalized, the consultant will continue to work with City 133 
staff to create the Economic Development Action Plan. This will include tasks at a more detailed 134
